test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Diesel) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which component in a multi-cylinder diesel engine directly drives the plunger-type fuel feed pump?
solution:
The correct answer is __F.I. pump camshaft.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• F.I. pump camshaft__ is a key component in the operation of multi-cylinder diesel engines.
 
• It directly drives the plunger-type fuel feed pump, ensuring accurate fuel delivery to the engine cylinders.
 
• The camshaft's role is to convert rotational motion from the crankshaft into linear motion required for pump operation.
 
• This ensures precise timing and efficient fuel injection for optimal engine performance.
 
• The fuel injection system relies heavily on the camshaft's mechanism for smooth and consistent operation.
 
• Proper maintenance of the camshaft and related components is crucial for engine longevity and efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Crankshaft:**

 
 
• It is a mechanical component that converts the linear motion of pistons into rotational motion.
 
• The crankshaft is essential for engine operation but does not directly drive the fuel feed pump.
 
 
 
• **Starter Motor:**
 
 
• The starter motor is responsible for initiating the engine's operation by cranking the engine.
 
• It is not directly connected to the operation of the fuel feed pump.
 
 
 
• **Alternator:**
 
 
• The alternator generates electrical power to charge the battery and supply power to electrical systems.
 
• It plays no role in driving the fuel feed pump.
